questions.section: Thrust from an engine that breathes air
questions.question: A jet engine flies at V∞ = 210 m/s with its nozzle expanded to the outside pressure. It takes in 60 kg/s of air, burns 1.2 kg/s of fuel, and its exhaust leaves at Ve = 540 m/s. What thrust does it make?
questions.explanation: T = (60 + 1.2) × 540 − 60 × 210 = 33,048 − 12,600 = 20,448 N, or 20.4 kN. 33.0 kN forgets the ram drag, the momentum the air had when it came in (60 × 210). 19.8 kN leaves out the fuel, which also leaves at Ve. 45.6 kN adds the incoming momentum instead of subtracting it.

questions.section: Thrust from an engine that breathes air
questions.question: In the thrust equation of an engine that breathes air, set the air mass flow to zero, so that everything leaving the nozzle was carried on board. What is left?
options: The rocket thrust equation of Chapter 4
A thrust of zero, since no air enters
Only the ram drag term, pointing backward
Only the pressure thrust term at the exit
questions.explanation: With no inflow, the ram drag term vanishes and the thrust is the mass flow of what was carried times the exit velocity, plus the pressure term: the rocket thrust equation of page 4.1. The thrust is not zero, because the carried mass still leaves at high speed; the ram drag disappears, it does not remain; and the momentum term stays beside the pressure term.

questions.section: Large air flow or fast exhaust
questions.question: An engine flies at V∞ = 220 m/s and its exhaust leaves at Ve = 770 m/s. What is its propulsive efficiency ηp?
questions.explanation: ηp = 2/(1 + Ve/V∞) = 2/(1 + 3.5) = 0.444, or 44%. 29% is V∞/Ve, the speed ratio upside down. 71% is 1 − V∞/Ve. 57% puts the speed added, Ve − V∞ = 550 m/s, in place of the exhaust speed: 2/(1 + 550/220).

questions.section: Large air flow or fast exhaust
questions.question: Two engines give the same thrust at the same flight speed. Which one wastes less energy in its wake?
options: The one that speeds up a larger air flow by less
The one with the faster exhaust, since it makes more thrust
Both waste the same, since their thrust is the same
The one that burns its fuel at a higher temperature
questions.explanation: The power left in the wake is one half of the air flow times the square of the speed added. For the same thrust, a larger flow needs a smaller speed increase, and the squared term makes its wake loss much smaller. Equal thrust does not mean equal waste; the exhaust speed does not add thrust by itself, the product of flow and speed increase does; and the combustion temperature is not part of the propulsive efficiency.

questions.question: In what order does the air pass the five stages of a turbojet?
options: Inlet, compressor, combustor, turbine, nozzle
Inlet, turbine, combustor, compressor, nozzle
Inlet, combustor, compressor, turbine, nozzle
Compressor, inlet, combustor, nozzle, turbine
questions.explanation: The inlet slows the air, the compressor raises its pressure, the combustor burns fuel in it, the turbine takes the work the compressor needs, and the nozzle turns what is left into exhaust speed. The turbine cannot come before the combustor: it needs the hot gas to drive the compressor. Fuel cannot burn before the air is compressed, and the inlet always comes first.

questions.question: Which parts of a single-spool turbojet carry the large rearward gas loads?
options: The turbine and the propelling nozzle
The compressor and the combustion chamber
The inlet and the compressor
The combustion chamber and the jet pipe
questions.explanation: The gas pushes rearward where its pressure falls: through the turbine and the propelling nozzle. The compressor and the combustion chamber carry the large forward loads, where the pressure rises or is highest. The inlet does not carry the rearward load, and the exhaust unit and jet pipe carry a small forward load.

questions.question: Why does an afterburner sit behind the turbine and not inside the main combustor?
options: The turbine blades limit how hot the gas reaching them can be
The turbine needs the extra fuel to turn the compressor
Fuel burns better in the slow, cold gas behind the turbine
The main combustor has no oxygen left to burn more fuel
questions.explanation: The spinning turbine blades sit in the hottest gas of the engine and limit its temperature. Behind the turbine there are no blades, so the gas can be heated further for a faster jet. The afterburner's fuel does not drive the turbine, which is ahead of it; the gas behind the turbine is still hot and burns the fuel less efficiently, not better; and the exhaust still has plenty of oxygen, which is what the afterburner uses.

questions.question: You must choose an engine type for a new aircraft. Which question decides first?
options: Which flight speed dominates the mission
Which engine type gives the most power
Which engine reaches the highest maximum speed
Which engine type is the lightest to install
questions.explanation: Each engine family works well only in a band of flight speed, so the speed the aircraft flies most of the time, often the cruise or the loiter, picks the family first. Choosing the most powerful engine type or the lightest skips that filter. Choosing for the maximum speed can give the wrong engine for the speed the aircraft spends most of its time at; the maximum speed is a check.
